title: Statement lines as text
prompt: The old statement printer takes amounts as text and needs only the day of each transaction. Write `solve(transactions)` so it returns `transaction_id`, `account_id`, `posted_on` and `amount_text`.
rules: `posted_on` is the date part of `posted_at`, as a `date`.
`amount_text` is `amount` as text, with both decimal places kept: 800.00 is `800.00`, not `800.0`.
A missing time or amount stays missing. Return the four columns, in that order, for every transaction, duplicates included.
hints: Two casts, each with an `alias`: one to `"date"`, one to `"string"`.
Casting a timestamp to a date keeps the day and drops the time.
Cast the decimal straight to text. Going through a `double` first loses the trailing zero.
starter:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F


def solve(transactions):
    # transaction_id, account_id, posted_on, amount_text
    return transactions
explanation: Two casts in one `select`: `transactions.select("transaction_id", "account_id", F.col("posted_at").cast("date").alias("posted_on"), F.col("amount").cast("string").alias("amount_text"))`. A decimal cast to text keeps its scale, so `800.00` stays `800.00`; cast to a `double` first and it prints as `800.0`. Casting the timestamp to `"string"` instead of `"date"` gives text with the time still on it. Missing values stay missing through both casts.
